You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 The Hanging Gardens In The Hanging Gardens, players compete to build the most beautiful garden for King Nebuchadnezzar II over four rounds Objective: Players act as gardeners for King Nebuchadnezzar II, building a beautiful hanging garden to please Queen Amytis. Over four rounds, players strategically select and place Garden cards, aiming to earn the most victory points by fulfilling objectives, arranging features, and optimizing card placement. Setup: Place the main gameboard and mini-board for the player count. Shuffle the deck of 75 Garden cards and place 12 face-up in 3 columns of 4 cards. Shuffle and stack Enhancement tiles face up in 3 piles. Randomly draw 4 Objective tiles and place them at the top of the board. Each player gets 1 Irrigation card. Each player takes 3 Gardeners, 4 Objective markers, 2 gold coins, and 4 tools (last player gets 1 extra tool). The last person to do yard work starts with the first-player marker. Gameplay Overview: The game is played over 4 rounds, with each round consisting of players using their 3 Gardeners to select and place 3 Garden cards. Turns proceed clockwise. Player Turn: Construct your garden by selecting a Garden card, placing it while following placement rules, and resolving any bonuses. Reveal a new Garden card by sliding cards down the column and adding a new card at the top. Buy an Enhancement tile (optional) to improve empty cards. Complete a Royal Objective (optional) by meeting specific conditions and placing an Objective marker. Scoring: At the end of 4 rounds, players score points for: Irrigation cards based on the specified layout. Largest connected groups of flowers in red, yellow, and blue. Groups of trees based on size. Animals placed on their preferred levels. Visitors' preferences for garden features. Completed Royal Objectives. Winner: The player with the most points wins. Ties are broken by tools and coins; tied players share victory if still tied. Key Strategy: Plan card placement to maximize connected groups, fulfill objectives, and optimize bonuses while managing resources like tools and gold coins. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary How to play 1 Construct your hanging garden (mandatory) a) Select a Garden card b) Place your Garden card c) Resolve your Garden card 2 Reveal a new Garden card (mandatory) 3 Buy a single Enhancement tile (optional) 4 Complete a single Royal Objective (optional) End of round The round ends when all players have placed all their Gardeners. Take back all your Gardeners and begin the next round. If you have played 4 rounds, you have all finished constructing your hanging gardens. Proceed to scoring. Scoring Scoring Score your victory points as follows: • Irrigation: Count the number of irrigated Garden cards in the places specified on your Irrigation card. Score the corresponding number of victory points. • Blooms: Only your largest connected group in each flower color (red, yellow and blue) scores. Gain 1 point per flower in those groups. • Trees: Score the number of points shown for your groups of connected trees of the same species. • Animals: Score the number of points for the level on which your animal is placed. Lions: like to lounge on level 1 Monkeys: like to play on level 2 Peacocks: like the calm on level 3 • Visitors: Score the points shown if the features your visitor wants to see are in your garden. • Royal Objectives: Score the same number of points as Royal Objectives you have completed. The winner is the player with the most victory points. If there is a tie, the winner is the player with the most tools and gold coins. If there is still a tie, the tied players both win. [Rating: 3/10] A tile drafting game where players place a worker, gaining a tile, and placing it onto their tableau. Each tile has different scoring mechanics. Once a player completes their 5/4/3 tiles per level, points are scored and the most points win.

[Rating: 4/10] Nice art, but does almost nothing to set itself apart from the vast array of abstract tile laying puzzle games that exist nowadays. It sits in a weird spot of being slightly more complex than many of them where I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for very new players, but it also doesn't really have that much going on either. Strange design.

[Rating: 5/10] What makes people 'design' games without any new idea?  I suppose they enjoy the process and it pleases their vanity.
